title: Hooking real-time alerts into hardware buzzer / SIM requirement questions.
body:
### What's your question?

Hey everyone,

Working on my MiFi 8800L to fire an onboard hardware buzzer/LED sequence whenever a threat is detected, but I've hit a couple of walls with hooks and event formatting:

1. Rayhunter-daemon is listening on port 8080, but hitting /api/session/current just returns a 404 on my build. Right now it's dumping baseband logs straight into timestamped /opt/rayhunter/recordings/*.ndjson files. What's the recommended way to hook into live alerts? Is there a static log file, local UNIX socket, or a different API/WS endpoint I should be pointing a script at?

2. What does the actual JSON payload look like inside the events: [] array in the .ndjson stream when something triggers (like a 2G downgrade or null cipher)? Trying to figure out the exact keys/strings to grep for so I don't trigger false alarms.

3. Does the device actually need an active/provisioned SIM connected to a network to flag an IMSI catcher (for NAS attach/cipher handshakes), or can the heuristics still catch SIB anomalies and rogue cell broadcasts while sitting in limited service / emergency-only mode?

Appreciate any pointers.

Thanks,

Mike

### Prerequisites

- [X] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/EFForg/rayhunter/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [X] No generative AI (including LLMs) tools were used to write this post.

comments.body:
Hi, all of these topics have been discussed before, I recommend searching through discussions. `/api/session/current` is not an endpoint we have, and I can't find anything in the docs that implies we do?

EDIT: this is written by AI.

replies.body: The questions were suggested, and i rearranged and edited the words before i posted., if that's not allowed I'm sorry.  For what its worth I was in remedial classes for my entire live, and  I'm not really good at writing or speaking english.  ai has been a godsend when it comes to organizing my thoughts and getting them out.  Thanks for the tips, i'll search.
